To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the use of a blind signal separation technique to estimate the power of a WDM channel is feasible; (ii) the technique can be applied to a real optical network, with no additional optical components; and (iii) it provides a power estimation that is comparable to that obtained using the standard technique.

(a) a novel blind source separation method for monitoring optical performance is proposed and validated, and (b) the proposed monitoring method is capable of providing a reliable estimate of the OSNR of WDM channels.
the proposed algorithm is able to monitor the quality of WDM channels using a single optical tap, with a low sampling rate, without any knowledge of the channel characteristics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a blind signal separation (BSS) algorithm for monitoring the quality of WDM channels in an optical network.
the development and application of blind signal separation methods to quality monitoring of optical signals in WDM systems.
the quality monitoring of optical channels in WDM systems using blind source separation methods.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is a very promising approach for optical performance monitoring of the 40-Gbit/s WDM system.
the blind separation method can be a powerful tool for optical performance monitoring.

we developed a new approach to the quality monitoring of WDM systems based on a novel method of signal separation.
we have shown how to use blind source separation methods for optical performance monitoring.
we have developed an efficient and robust technique for monitoring the quality of the channels in a WDM system.

it is possible to achieve high performance with a simple and inexpensive receiver, which is a key requirement for the deployment of WDM-PONs.
